ambiguities.description: The table columns read 'Flight cycle (FC) limit from the effective date of this AD' (also in Tables 2 and 3). The text does not say whether the cycles are counted on the part or on the engine it is installed in. The two counts differ if the part has moved between engines since the effective date. The record uses the part count.
readings: Cycles accumulated by the part since the effective date, on any engine.
Flight cycles of the engine in which the part is installed since the effective date.

ambiguities.description: 'AUSI inspected parts installed on or after November 1, 2023' are not identified by P/N or S/N. The text does not say whether this covers only hubs listed in Table 1 of the NMSB and PW SI or any AUSI inspected HPT hub. The 4,000 FCs are also not stated as part or engine cycles.
readings: Only hubs with S/Ns in the NMSB or PW SI tables referenced by Table 1 to paragraph (g)(1).
Any HPT 1st-stage or 2nd-stage hub that has had an AUSI and was installed on or after November 1, 2023.

ambiguities.description: 'Part eligible for installation' is defined in terms of an 'HPT 1st-stage disk or HPT 2nd-stage disk', while the actions use 'hub', and no P/N is printed. Eligibility turns on the S/N not being listed in either service document, or on the part not having been removed from service per this AD. A listed part that passed AUSI is therefore eligible but remains subject to (g)(2). No P/N-based clearing is recorded.
readings: 'Disk' and 'hub' denote the same HPT 1st-stage and 2nd-stage parts.
'Disk' denotes a different part designation than 'hub'.

ambiguities.description: Table 1 to paragraph (g)(1) and Table 2 to paragraph (g)(4) print only a 'Yes' (previously operated in high-thrust model engine) row for parts listed in PW SI No. 189F-23. They give no compliance time for a PW SI-listed part that has not so operated.
readings: Every PW SI-listed part is treated as previously operated in a high-thrust model engine (the SI applies only to the V2531-E5, a high-thrust model per (h)(3)).
No compliance time is stated for such a part.

governing_document.reason: Final rule 2024-12594 (Amendment 39-22764) is the only document in the thread. No correction republishes its regulatory text, so its regulatory text controls.

notes: Applicability (c) is by engine model only. Every action is limited to hubs whose S/Ns appear in IAE AG NMSB V2500-ENG-72-0720 Tables 1-4 or PW SI No. 189F-23 Tables 1-2; those lists are not printed in the AD.

The text states that PW SI No. 189F-23 only applies to the IAE AG V2531-E5 Model engine. The actions on SI-listed parts are not restricted by model in the regulatory text, so no model restriction is recorded.

How the actions fit together: a listed Table 1 part with no AUSI gets the AUSI under (g)(1), then removal under (g)(2). An AUSI inspected part installed on or after November 1, 2023 is removed under (g)(2). An AUSI inspected part installed prior to November 1, 2023 (per Table 2) is removed under (g)(4). Parts listed in NMSB Tables 3 and 4 are removed under (g)(5) without AUSI.

AUSI procedures are Accomplishment Instructions paragraph 5. (1st-stage hub) and paragraph 6. (2nd-stage hub) of the applicable service document. These are procedure-only material and are not recorded as dependencies.
Paragraph (f): comply within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
The preamble describes this AD as an interim action. The FAA estimates that 116 U.S.-registry engines are affected.

relationships.description: Compliance with paragraph (g)(1) of this AD satisfies the requirements of AD 2022-02-09 (Amendment 39-21906, 87 FR 7029, February 8, 2022). The text does not print that AD's Federal Register document number.
Paragraph (b) states that this AD is related to AD 2022-02-09, Amendment 39-21906 (87 FR 7029, February 8, 2022).
